title: HydraScript project configuration
description: Schema for hydraconfig.json. Keys the current runner ignores are still listed, and their description says so, so an editor never promises behaviour the tool does not have.

$schema.description: Points at this file. Editors use it for completion and validation.

name.description: Project name, used in scaffolding output.

base.description: Asset URL prefix. "sub", "/sub" and "/sub/" are equivalent. An absolute URL (a CDN) is kept verbatim.

outputDir.description: Directory the build writes to, relative to the project root.

routes.description: Where the file-based router looks for pages. A string is the directory; `false` turns the router off; an object may carry `dir`. Default `./src/pages`.

mode.description: Overrides the build mode. Usually left to hydra dev / hydra build.

tailwind.description: Turns ON Tailwind for this project and merges into its config. `content` is extended with index.html and src/**/*. Tailwind is not a dependency of the framework; a project that sets this key must install `tailwindcss` (and normally `postcss`, `autoprefixer`) itself.

port.description: Port to serve on. `--port N` on dev/preview overrides it.

host.description: Bind address. Defaults to loopback; `--host 0.0.0.0` or this key makes the server reachable from the network.

proxy.description: Path-prefix to backend mapping, matched like Vite's server.proxy. A backend that is down returns 502, not a crash.

bodyLimit.description: Largest request body an API route or action will read. Default 1048576 (1 MiB). Either bytes (`1048576`) or a size string (`"10mb"`, `"512kib"`); a string is converted once at startup, because a string compared against a byte count silently removes the limit. A bigger body is answered with 413 and `Connection: close`, never a dropped socket.

rateLimit.description: Per-IP rate limiting for the built-in server (dev/preview/serve). When enabled, requests exceeding `max` within `windowMs` receive 429 Too Many Requests with a `Retry-After` header.

headers.description: Extra response headers, added to every answer. The framework sets nosniff, Referrer-Policy, X-Frame-Options and Permissions-Policy itself; this is where a project adds its own, most usefully Content-Security-Policy. Applied to static files, SSR, API routes, actions, the data endpoint and error pages alike. `{nonce}` is replaced per request with a fresh nonce, so a policy can cover the inline hydration JSON.

allowedOrigins.description: Which Origins may POST to an action or an API route (CSRF gate). List the site's public origins, e.g. ["https://example.com"]. Without it the check compares Origin to the Host header, which a DNS-rebinding attacker can make agree — so set this on anything real.

oneOf.description: Comma-separated list of proxy addresses whose X-Forwarded-For is believed.

trustProxy.description: Which peers may set X-Forwarded-For. OFF by default: the header is written by the client, so trusting it unconditionally lets a caller pick its own rate-limit bucket (and grow the limiter’s memory without bound). Set true (or list the proxy addresses) only when the server really runs behind a proxy that overwrites the header.

jsxInJs.description: Treat .js files as JSX. Set false if a .js file in your project contains something esbuild would misread as JSX.

target.description: NOT USED YET. Accepted and validated, but the current runner always compiles for react-18 and does not switch on this value.

strict.description: NOT USED YET. Accepted and validated, but no compile-time semantic checks exist yet, so setting this changes nothing. Do not rely on it to catch mistakes.

ssg.description: Pre-render every static route to its own HTML file. ON by default (the code treats anything but an explicit false as on); `HYDRA_NO_SSG=1` skips it for one build.

ssr.description: Server-render dynamic routes on each request. ON by default; `hydra init` writes it here when the project asked for SSR, and `false` makes a dynamic route answer with the client shell (which `hydra serve` reports).

sourcemap.description: Emit source maps for the client bundle. OFF by default: a map carries the application's source in `sourcesContent`, and `dist/` is what gets uploaded.

target.description: What the artifact is for. `static` writes HTML/JS/CSS only and does NOT serve src/api or src/middleware.hys (it lists every dropped route at build time). `node` also includes the API routes, middleware, loaders and actions. `hydra build --target` overrides this for one build. There are deliberately only two targets.

clean.description: Empty the output directory before writing. ON by default, so a route deleted from the source stops being served; set false only when the directory holds files this build does not own.

root.description: NOT USED YET. Accepted and validated, but the runner always reads sources from ./src.

entries.description: NOT USED YET. Accepted and validated, but the entrypoint is always the first of src/main.hyx, src/main.hsx, src/index.hyx, src/index.hsx that exists.

styling.description: Which CSS pipeline this project uses. An array of PostCSS plugin names (or a relative path to one): `"styling": ["autoprefixer"]`. Ignored when a `postcss.config.*` file exists, because that config is the project speaking. When neither is present, a top-level `tailwind` key or a tailwind.config turns on Tailwind + autoprefixer; otherwise the stylesheet runs through plain PostCSS (autoprefixer only if installed). There is no `type` here on purpose: the two shapes below are the whole value, and a `type: object` beside `oneOf` rejected the array form the README documents.

oneOf.description: PostCSS plugin names or relative paths.

tailwind.description: `{"styling": {"tailwind": true}}` — what `hydra init --styling=tailwind` writes. Same meaning as the top-level `tailwind` key.

oneOf.description: Same, wrapped in an object. `hydra init` writes `{"tailwind": true}` here for the Tailwind pipeline.

ssr.description: Set false to disable server rendering of dynamic routes in dev/preview/serve. A dynamic route then answers with the client shell, and `hydra serve` reports why.

types.description: TypeScript declaration output. `hydra init --types` writes `{"emit": true}`; `hydra types` also writes them on demand.

emit.description: Write `routes.d.ts` and the `hydra` module declaration during build.
